messages:
Sam H: Quick thread — we need a clear compatibility matrix for model-variant fallbacks that covers more than just logits/latency. tokenizer differences, context-length behavior, and tool-calling parity are causing silent breakages when we route across tiers/regions.
Maria G: +1. I did a quick tokenization diff between main-en-v2 and distilled-en-compat on our LLM-samples set. ~1.2% of prompts got different token boundaries which changes truncation behavior and sometimes breaks function-call parsing. Example: 
```
prompt: \"Summarize the repo and call repo_browser.open(path=\"/src/main\")\"
main-en-v2 tokens: [.., 'repo', '_', 'browser', '.', 'open', ..]
distilled-en-compat tokens: [.., 'repo_browser', '.', 'open', ..]
```
Maria G: That leads to function args being smashed into one token on the fallback variant, parser fails, returns no function call -> user sees unstructured text. :exclamation:
Lee C: We should instrument three telemetry counters immediately: `tokenizer_mismatch_count`, `function_call_parse_errors`, `context_truncation_rate_by_route`. Those give us signal per-region, per-tier. Also add a histogram of token_delta_per_prompt so we can threshold routes that are unsafe.
Aj Patel: UX question — when console admins enable fallback routing (e.g., dedicated->hosted spillover), should we show a compatibility score/warning? If we put that behind a tooltip, customers won't notice until they hit an error. Maybe a preflight check + tooltip + opt-out toggle for specific routes.
Nina R: Also: billing. If fallback variants tokenize differently, per-token billing will differ. Need to add an estimated token multiplier to any automated routing decisions so we don't silently double-bill customers who expect same cost bracket.
Sam H: Agree on telemetry + billing. For the compatibility matrix, propose columns: `model_variant`, `tokenizer_family`, `avg_token_ratio`, `max_context`, `tool_calling_supported`, `tool_call_shape_match`, `notes`. We need owners for each cell. Who wants to own the tokenizer parity checks? @Maria G?
Maria G: I can own tokenization diffs and produce an automated nightly report. Plan: run 10k sampled prompts, compute token_ratio and a tokenization_diff_examples bucket. Will surface top 20 failing examples in the report.
Lee C: Runtime can add function_call_parse_errors and truncation_rate to existing per-route metrics. For alerts: if `function_call_parse_errors` spikes > 0.5% on fallback route for 10m, auto-disable that fallback and page oncall. We need a safe fallback-off policy.
Aj Patel: For rollout UX: console should show a red badge if selected fallback has any `tool_calling_supported=false` or `tokenizer_family` mismatch. Options: (1) Allow but warn, (2) Block (force disable), (3) Auto-truncate/prefix-transform to mitigate tokenizer diffs. Which is preferred?
Nina R: From contracts/legal, we must not change customers' responses silently. Blocking or explicit opt-in is safer. Auto-transform is risky unless we prove equivalence.
Maria G: For mitigation experiments we can try a prefix tokenization shim: if token_ratio > 1.15 or tokenizer_family differs, run a preflight transform: `encode_with_primary -> map_tokens -> decode -> send to fallback` — but that's expensive and might shift semantics.
Sam H: Ok — next practical step: build the compatibility matrix skeleton and a gating policy. I sketched a small matrix example: 
```json
[
  {"model_variant":"main-en-v2","tokenizer_family":"bpe-v1","avg_token_ratio":"1.00","max_context":"8192","tool_calling_supported":"true","tool_call_shape_match":"true","notes":"primary"},
  {"model_variant":"distilled-en-compat","tokenizer_family":"bpe-v2","avg_token_ratio":"0.87","max_context":"4096","tool_calling_supported":"false","tool_call_shape_match":"false","notes":"fast, smaller vocab - not tool-safe"}
]
```
Sam H: We should store that in config + surface in console.
Aj Patel: Add `tool_call_shape` column (JSON schema fingerprint) — some models return different function-arg structures (e.g., positional vs named). Also add `recommended_action` (warn/block/auto-transform).
Lee C: For tests: create a small eval harness with ~200 function-call prompts, from all supported tool schemas, run across variants, compute `function_call_fidelity` (exact match on parsed function name + args). If fidelity < 99% block fallback for production routes.
Nina R: Ops question — if a customer is on Dedicated (tier=A) and we fallback to hosted region B, do we need to mirror data residency controls? If fallback violates contractual region constraints we must not route. Add `region_compliance_ok` column.
Maria G: I'll add region tests and token diffs. I'll push a prototype nightly report to `#eng-platform` channel and attach a CSV.
deploy-bot: Scheduled rollout: fallback-compat-checker v0.1 will start canary at 2026-11-02T03:00Z and run against 5% traffic for 2 hours. See runbook: https://staging-console/redwood/fallback-checker :rocket:
Sam H: Owners and next steps: Maria -> tokenizer diffs + nightly report; Lee -> telemetry metrics + alert; Aj -> console UX badge + gating options; Nina -> billing + compliance matrix; Sam -> matrix schema + config PR. Follow-up sync on Friday 13:30 PT. If anyone wants to add columns to the matrix please comment here. :thumbsup:
